answer: Each identity drills one core and locks a 70-credit core bond. The top layer must be a quartz band, and the log goes on the column board. Below it lies a velvet seam, and below that a ripple bed; anyone can check the order against the column and that no log repeats. The first core costs 40; the k-th core from one source costs 40+5(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 5,035 and 1,000 cores cost 2,537,500 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-core ring fails because a rented log is already on the board, and a duplicate burns both bonds. An honest agent drills once, pays 40, and recovers the bond after check.
